timeline.tweet: Nothing wrong with rambling. I find myself doing that too often.

I took this week to think over why I felt burnt out. Why I felt so tired and exhausted from streaming. One part was definitely the physical lack of good sleep, but the second was emotional exhaustion. I cared too much. Spoke up too much. Took things too seriously. I lost the joy

I am socially awkward because I feel others secretly dislike me and find me annoying. I constantly critique my interactions with others to make sure I wasn't being a douche. If you have this same feeling, remember that it isn't true. Don't be afraid to express yourself. Be You.

I was taught from an early age that crying was the only unacceptable emotional release. Expressing anger, fighting, destruction, far more negative things were seen as more appropriate for a boy. I just swallow it. Let it build up, and once every few months around 2AM, cry.

But then I remember, it took a pandemic for me to be with my family more. It took a pandemic for execs to embrace remote working. It took a pandemic to help my depression. So what happens when its over? Will I just go back to how things were? My stress and my depression?
I call this one "separation anxiety"
